chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the virgin girl whom her father maries off without her consent, he (peace be upon him) said: She has no authority with her father; if he marries her off, the marriage is valid, even if she dislikes it.

He (peace be upon him) said: And he was asked about a man who wanted to marry off his sister. He said: He should consult her; if she remains silent, it is her consent, but if she refuses, he should not marry her off.
ai.seo_question: Does a father need his virgin daughter's consent for marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the fiqh of marriage consent (rida) by distinguishing between a virgin (bikr), whose father’s authority is paramount and makes the marriage valid even against her will, and a mature woman (thayyib), where consultation is required and silence constitutes consent. This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly view on the balance between paternal guardianship (wilayah) and individual agency, rooted in the Prophet’s practice and juristic interpretation of marital validity.
